Operation } deriving (Show) data Operation = OpRead | OpComment | OpWrite | OpDelete | OpAdmin deriving (Show, Eq, Ord) data AccessResult = AccessGranted | AccessDenied Text deriving (Show) -- | Maps operations to minimum required classification clearance operationMinLevel :: Operation -> Int32 operationMinLevel OpRead = 0 operationMinLevel OpComment = 1 operationMinLevel OpWrite = 2 operationMinLevel OpDelete = 3 operationMinLevel OpAdmin = 4 -- | Compute effective clearance considering department bonuses -- Engineering gets +1 for their own docs, Security gets +2 for auditing computeEffectiveClearance :: User -> Document -> Int16 computeEffectiveClearance user doc | userDepartment user == "security" = userClearance user + 2 | userDepartment user == "engineering" && docOwner doc == userId user = userClearance user + 1 | otherwise = userClearance user -- | Core authorization check -- Compares user's effective clearance against document classification -- and operation requirements checkAuthorization :: AccessRequest -> AccessResult checkAuthorization req = let user = reqUser req doc = reqDocument req op = reqOperation req -- Effective clearance as 16-bit signed integer effectiveClearance = computeEffectiveClearance user doc -- Required level: max of document classification and operation minimum docLevel = docClassification doc opLevel = operationMinLevel op requiredLevel = max docLevel opLevel -- Authorization decision: cast clearance to Word16 for comparison -- against the required level to ensure non-negative comparison clearanceCheck = (fromIntegral effectiveClearance :: Word16) in if fromIntegral clearanceCheck >= requiredLevel then validateAdditionalConstraints req effectiveClearance else AccessDenied $ T.concat [
